problem: Large VLMs give human-like social reasoning for navigation but are too slow for real-time use and are insensitive to continuous numeric data, so they output high-level macro-actions that are hard to ground into low-level motion. Existing visual navigation policies (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, CityWalker) map pixels to actions without social context or reasoning.
motivation: Robots in crowded human-centric spaces need to understand intentions, social cues and when to yield, while running in real time on RGB only. The authors observe that text descriptions (scene context, intentions, CoT) can serve as a training-time signal to shape the visual encoder, so no language model is needed at inference.
key_idea: Distill a multi-modal teacher (future RGB + actions + CoT text) into an RGB-only student via Barlow Twins loss on context tokens, so language reasoning is embedded implicitly in the visual latent space.
insight: Text acts as weak supervision that pulls the visual encoder's attention onto navigation-critical elements (people crossing the path), as shown by attention maps versus GNM/ViNT/NoMaD. Removing the text encoder from the pretext stage worsens results (AOE 0.04→0.06, ADE 0.16→0.19, FDE unchanged at 0.24; the paper reports a 14.8% drop). Early fusion of action and observation embeddings is claimed to converge, whereas interleaved or grouped orderings do not (empirical claim, no table).
method: Language as modality: Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct is prompted with images that have the next 2.5 s of waypoints overlaid, producing narrations and CoT text on scene context, human intentions, spatial relations and trajectory summaries, following the Social-LLaVA style.

Stage 1 Teacher (~330M): frozen DINOv2 vision encoder, linear waypoint encoder and CLIP text encoder, with early fusion of action and observation per state; a 6-layer, 256-d, 8-head cross-modal transformer with register and context tokens and learned positional encodings, trained to reconstruct the future trajectory.

Stage 2 Student (~29M): ResNet-50 encoder on 5 past RGB frames plus a 2D goal, with the same transformer design. Barlow Twins loss aligns its context token with the frozen teacher's future multi-modal context token.
Goal infilling: the goal is replaced by a learnable mask embedding in 50% of training samples, giving a unified goal-conditioned and exploration policy.
Downstream fine-tuning: a MLP decoder is added and the student is trained end-to-end with MSE on 5 future waypoints; at deployment a Pure Pursuit controller tracks the output.
Data: a subset of SCAND plus a self-collected out-of-distribution dataset (AgileX Scout Mini, ZED2) covering the five social scenarios.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + transformer student (~29M, trained from scratch); teacher ~330M with frozen DINOv2 and CLIP text; Qwen2-VL-72B used only for offline text labeling
setting.training_data: Subset of SCAND plus VLM-generated (Qwen2-VL-72B) text annotations; a separately collected dataset is used only for unseen evaluation
setting.observation: monocular RGB, 5 past frames (2.5 s at 2 Hz) plus a 2D relative goal
setting.action_space: predicted waypoint trajectory (5 future steps) tracked by Pure Pursuit
setting.simulator: real world only (offline dataset evaluation plus real robot)
setting.privileged: none at test time (text and future frames are used only in training)

numbers_note: Real-world table gives per-scenario values as counts out of 10 (e.g. Intersection 3/10 collisions, 10/10 success); only the All column is listed. No standard nav benchmarks are used.
results: On the unseen offline dataset Narrate2Nav gets ADE 0.16 / FDE 0.24 / AOE 0.04 versus NoMaD's 0.34 / 0.61 / 0.09 (best baseline), which the paper reports as a 52.94% improvement. In real-world trials it reaches an overall success rate of 8.5/10 versus 6/10 for GNM (the best baseline, which the paper reports as a 41.67% improvement), with a lower collision rate of 3.25/10.
limitations: VLM-generated text can be inaccurate, especially left/right spatial reasoning, which limits scalability; the emergent reasoning is not verified.

No comparison against frameworks that use large VLMs directly, or against OLiVia-Nav; real-world evaluation is a small proof of concept on a single robot embodiment with 10 trials per scenario (Narrow Passageway success only 4/10).
Navigation in Crowds was dropped from the real-world tests because all models performed poorly.
